title: Internal tensor multiplication is the unit-normalized composition comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided monoidal category with coequalizers, such that tensoring on either side preserves colimits. Let $R,S,T$ be commutative monoid objects and $\varphi:R\to S$, $\psi:S\to T$ morphisms of monoid objects. Use the internal module categories and coequalizer scalar-extension functors of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Write $A=\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}$, $B=\operatorname{Ext}_{\psi}$, $D=\operatorname{Ext}_{\psi\varphi}$ and $U=\operatorname{Res}_{\psi\varphi}$. Identify $\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}\operatorname{Res}_{\psi}$ with $U$ by the canonical comparison that is the identity on underlying objects and arrows. Equip $BA\dashv U$ with the composite scalar-extension adjunction transported along this comparison, and $D\dashv U$ with the direct scalar-extension adjunction. Denote their units by $\eta^{BA}$ and $\eta^D$, and let $u:BA\xrightarrow{\sim}D$ be the unique unit-compatible isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation].

There is a natural isomorphism $m_0:BA\xrightarrow{\sim}D$ induced on the defining coequalizers by multiplication in $T$, with component and inverse given in symbolic tensor notation by
$$m_{0,M}:T\otimes_S(S\otimes_RM)\longrightarrow T\otimes_RM,\quad t\otimes(s\otimes x)\longmapsto t\psi(s)\otimes x,$$
$$m_{0,M}^{-1}:t\otimes x\longmapsto t\otimes(1\otimes x).$$
These formulas mean maps induced from $T\otimes S\otimes M$ and $T\otimes M$ through the relative-tensor coequalizers, with the monoidal associators and unitors inserted; they do not assume that $\mathcal C$ is concrete. For every $R$-module object $M$,
$$U(m_{0,M})\circ\eta^{BA}_M=\eta^D_M.$$
As specified natural isomorphisms, $m_0=u$ (equivalently, $m_0$ is the inverse of the source-library $\operatorname{Mod.extendScalarsComp}(\varphi,\psi)$).

proof.text: Fix $M$ and put $P=S\otimes_RM$, $Q=T\otimes_SP$, $H=T\otimes_RM$. Write their coequalizer projections as $q:S\otimes M\to P$, $p:T\otimes P\to Q$, $r:T\otimes M\to H$. These are the objects, actions and maps of [def-sfb-modobj-extension]. By [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction] their unit maps are $a=q(\eta_S\otimes M)\lambda_M^{-1}:M\to P$, $b=p(\eta_T\otimes P)\lambda_P^{-1}:P\to Q$, and $c=r(\eta_T\otimes M)\lambda_M^{-1}:M\to H$. They are respectively $R$-, $S$-, and $R$-linear into the appropriate restrictions. Restriction is the identity on underlying arrows by [def-sfb-modobj-restriction]. The composite Hom bijection sends a $T$-linear $f:Q\to N$ first to $fb$ and then to $fba$; evaluating at $f=\mathrm{id}_Q$ shows that the transported composite unit has underlying arrow $ba$, while the direct unit has underlying arrow $c$.

source.place: Compatibility with composition: coequalizer notation and the two unit maps. Source-library ExtendScalars.lean:321-337, 348-350, 413-435.

proof.text:
We will use the identities $q=\gamma_P(S\otimes a)$, $p=\gamma_Q(T\otimes b)$, and $r=\gamma_H(T\otimes c)$. Here is their direct verification, simultaneously for any one of the three extensions $F=V\otimes_W L$, with projection $e$ and unit $d=e(\eta_V\otimes L)\lambda_L^{-1}$. The first-factor action specified in [def-sfb-modobj-extension] means
$$\gamma_F(V\otimes e)=e(\mu_V\otimes L)\alpha_{V,V,L}^{-1}.$$
Consequently
$$\gamma_F(V\otimes d)=e(\mu_V\otimes L)\alpha_{V,V,L}^{-1}(V\otimes(\eta_V\otimes L))(V\otimes\lambda_L^{-1})=e.$$
The last equality uses the right-unit axiom $\mu_V(V\otimes\eta_V)=\rho_V$ from [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] and the monoidal triangle identity. Thus these identities are computations with the actual coequalizer and action morphisms, requiring no generators in a concrete category.

source.place: Compatibility with composition: insertion of the unit followed by the induced first-factor action. Compare ExtendScalars.lean:223-229, 341-346.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to the two adjunctions in the statement, after the stipulated restriction comparison, using the identity isomorphism of their common right adjoint $U$. It gives a natural isomorphism $v:BA\xrightarrow{\sim}D$ with $v_Mba=c$ on underlying arrows. All three extension adjunctions exist by [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction]: $R$ is commutative for $A,D$, $S$ is commutative for $B$, and the ambient coequalizer and tensor-preservation assumptions are exactly theirs. No closedness or equalizers are being assumed. The comparison of restrictions changes neither underlying objects nor arrows, so the displayed equation is exactly its required unit equation, rather than an equation for a different adjunction.

source.place: Compatibility with composition: common-right-adjoint comparison and its unit equation (Stacks Categories Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints).

proof.text:
Let $h=v_Mb:P\to H$. It is $S$-linear for the restriction of the $T$-action on $H$: $b$ is $S$-linear and $v_M$ is $T$-linear, hence $S$-linear after [def-sfb-modobj-restriction]. Also $ha=c$. Using the identity for $q$ in step 2 and the definition of a module morphism in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], we obtain
$$hq=h\gamma_P(S\otimes a)=\gamma_H(\psi\otimes h)(S\otimes a)=\gamma_H(\psi\otimes c).$$
Expand $c=r(\eta_T\otimes M)\lambda_M^{-1}$ and the first-factor action on $H$ from [def-sfb-modobj-extension]. Associator and unitor naturality give the typed equality
$$\gamma_H(\psi\otimes c)=r(\mu_T\otimes M)\alpha_{T,T,M}^{-1}\bigl(\psi\otimes((\eta_T\otimes M)\lambda_M^{-1})\bigr)=r(\psi\otimes M).$$
Indeed, move $\psi$ through the associator by naturality and use $\mu_T(\psi\otimes\eta_T)=\psi\rho_S$, followed by the monoidal triangle identity, exactly as in step 2. Thus $hq=r(\psi\otimes M)$ is an equality of maps $S\otimes M\to H$.

source.place: Compatibility with composition: determine the intermediate S-linear map from its value at the unit.

proof.text:
By $T$-linearity of $v_M$ and step 2,
$$v_Mp=v_M\gamma_Q(T\otimes b)=\gamma_H(T\otimes h).$$
Precomposing with $T\otimes q$ and using step 4 and the induced action on $H$ yields the fully typed formula
$$v_Mp(T\otimes q)=r(\mu_T\otimes M)((T\otimes\psi)\otimes M)\alpha_{T,S,M}^{-1}:T\otimes(S\otimes M)\to H.$$
This is the multiplication map required for $m_{0,M}$. It therefore factors through both defining coequalizers, with factor $v_M$; existence and $T$-linearity are already provided by this factor, so no elementwise balancing assertion is needed. This factor is unique: $q$ and $p$ are coequalizer maps, and $T\otimes q$ is also a coequalizer map by the assumed preservation of colimits. For a coequalizer map $e$, if $fe=ge$, its universal property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] says that $f$ and $g$ are the same factor of that coequalizing arrow. Apply this first to $T\otimes q$ and then to $p$. Thus the natural isomorphism $v$ is exactly the coequalizer-induced multiplication comparison $m_0$.

source.place: Compatibility with composition: multiplication on the double coequalizer and uniqueness of its factor.

proof.text:
Write $w_M=v_M^{-1}$. Composing $v_Mba=c$ with $w_M$ gives $w_Mc=ba$. Since $w_M$ is a morphism of $T$-modules, the identities of step 2 give
$$w_Mr=w_M\gamma_H(T\otimes c)=\gamma_Q(T\otimes w_Mc)=\gamma_Q(T\otimes b)(T\otimes a)=p(T\otimes a).$$
After substituting $a$, this is the actual arrow
$$w_Mr=p(T\otimes q)(T\otimes(\eta_S\otimes M))(T\otimes\lambda_M^{-1}):T\otimes M\to Q.$$
It proves the claimed symbolic inverse $t\otimes x\mapsto t\otimes(1\otimes x)$, with all unitors displayed. The direct coequalizer universal property determines its factor uniquely. The two inverse identities hold because $w_M$ is the inverse component of $v$; this proves them as internal module morphisms, including any case with zero objects.

source.place: Compatibility with composition: inverse from insertion of the unit and the inverse normalization equation.

proof.text: The component calculation identifies $m_0=v$ as a natural transformation; thus its naturality and the natural inverse just computed follow from the natural isomorphism supplied in step 3. Moreover $U(m_{0,M})\eta^{BA}_M=\eta^D_M$, since the underlying arrows are $v_Mba=c$ and module morphisms are their underlying arrows with the linearity equation of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] gives $m_0=u$ as specified natural isomorphisms. Finally the source-library definition at ExtendScalars.lean:463-467 is the comparison from the direct adjunction to the transported composite adjunction. Its unit equation is the reverse one, so its inverse has $U(-)\eta^{BA}=\eta^D$ and is $m_0$ by the same uniqueness. The direction is therefore the inverse of $\operatorname{Mod.extendScalarsComp}(\varphi,\psi)$ as asserted.
